The proof verifies angle and normalization limits, threshold boundaries and the explicit rational witness. The included exact-rational checker passed 12,578 comparisons plus 15 independent numerical ray checks. Finite checks corroborate but are not a proof of the universal theorem.

originality.rationale: The full texts of arXiv:2607.28768v1 and arXiv:2608.27491v1, the relevant sections of arXiv:1512.07289v1, and the complete public RESULT of the closest published width-spectrum theorem were materially inspected. The first two establish tangent-angle structure and cone-measure transfer but not radial-distance distributional inversion. The third studies distributions of projections and sections. The closest published gap-reconstruction theorem uses widths in random directions and requires central symmetry; it does not assert the present all-tangential boundary- or area-sampled radial inverse theorem. Both complete radial laws, the knot inversion, and sharp dihedral-fiber count have distinct hypotheses and observables. Historical completeness is not guaranteed.

value.rationale: The radial distance to the canonical incenter of a uniformly selected point is a natural unlabeled geometric observable. Exact inverse identifiability is classified across every tangential n-gon, not one artificial finite slice: both arclength and area sampling recover the same complete angle multiset and inradius, while the precise remaining ambiguity is the multiset dihedral-orbit count and is generically (n-1)!/2. Four sides are the first generic nonuniqueness threshold. This is a complete boundary-of-identification statement in inverse stochastic geometry with explicit formulas, a constructive witness, and future bearing on noisy distance tomography. It neither claims global reconstruction of arbitrary convex sets nor generic classical cone sampling as new.
